summary.text: Neptune is the eighth and farthest known planet from the Sun, an ice giant with no well-defined solid surface.
Unexpected changes in Uranus's orbit led astronomers to predict it mathematically, and Galle then saw it by telescope in 1846.
It has the strongest sustained winds of any planet, up to 2,100 km/h, and Voyager 2 in 1989 is the only spacecraft to visit.

items.prompt: How did astronomers first work out where to point telescopes to find Neptune?

options.label: They followed a wobble in the Sun's motion
They spotted a moving speck on old photographs
They calculated it from odd changes in Uranus's orbit
They traced the path of a passing comet

items.explain: Unexpected changes in the orbit of Uranus suggested an unknown planet, and its position was mathematically predicted.

items.prompt: Galileo drew Neptune's position twice in the early 1600s, yet is not credited with discovering it. Why?

options.label: He took it for a fixed star
His drawings were lost for centuries
He thought it was a moon of Jupiter
He never published his notes

items.explain: Galileo seems to have mistaken Neptune for a fixed star, so he is not credited with its discovery.

items.prompt: A British astronomer recorded Neptune a year before Galle did but did not realise it. What went wrong?

options.label: Neptune was too dim for his small telescope
He was waiting for Adams's position first
Neptune had not yet moved against the stars
Outdated star maps and poor observing technique

items.explain: Challis had observed it earlier, but out-of-date star maps and poor observing techniques meant he failed to recognise the observations.

items.prompt: Uranus can look featureless for long periods. What is Neptune's atmosphere like by comparison?

options.label: Just as seasonal and blank
Active, with consistently visible weather patterns
Calm, because it is so far from the Sun
Frozen still, with no wind

items.explain: In contrast to the strongly seasonal atmosphere of Uranus, Neptune's has active and consistently visible weather patterns.

items.prompt: Neptune looks faintly blue. What contributes to that colour?

options.label: Oceans of liquid water on its surface
Sunlight bouncing off ice caps
Traces of methane in its outermost regions
Ammonia crystals in its upper air

items.explain: Along with Rayleigh scattering, traces of methane in the outermost regions make Neptune appear faintly blue.

items.prompt: Why are Neptune's cloud tops among the coldest places in the Solar System?

options.label: It is very far from the Sun
Its core is as cold as its clouds
Its winds carry all heat to space
It has no atmosphere to hold warmth

items.explain: Because of its great distance from the Sun, its outer atmosphere is one of the coldest places, while its centre is about 5,400 K.
